similar_scenes.name: Doom, super-doom y stoner rock
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: El doom (exageración lenta, gótica y barroca de los grooves de Black Sabbath) crece en Inglaterra: Paradise Lost, Cathedral (las largas suites líricas de Forest Of Equilibrium), My Dying Bride y Electric Wizard, que infla la pesadez hasta que la música ya no fluye, solo retumba (Come My Fanatics, Dopethrone); Orange Goblin, Katatonia. El «super-doom» de los Melvins sigue en Seattle con Earth (drones colosales entre La Monte Young y monstruos extraterrestres), Karp, Sunn, y el «sludgecore» del Sur (Eyehategod, Harvey Milk). El stoner rock: Kyuss, Queens Of The Stone Age, Sleep, Fu Manchu, Monster Magnet, Wellwater Conspiracy, Boris.

podcast.title: Foundations from Josh Homme
podcast.body: Josh Homme's signature "chunky, riffy sound" is recognized as a significant foundational element of the genre now known as Stoner Rock. "His signature chunky riffy sound is a big part of the foundations of what we now call Stoner Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Popular Term for Kyuss's Genre
podcast.body: This genre name became widely associated with the fuzzy guitar music pioneered by Kyuss, despite Josh Homme's personal dislike for the term. "But the one that really stuck was Stoner Rock. Josh grew to hate that term."
